title: has one part per row
why: A part whose row was renamed in the walkthrough would go unwalked with nothing said.

title: puts each part
why: A part whose result names no table row would be written nowhere, or into the wrong cell.

title: types no sentence
why: A sentence typed into a script is heard against itself, not against the app.

title: compares letters and digits only
why: Without whole-word matching, unchecked would be heard as checked.

title: appends to a cell
why: A script that overwrites a cell erases a person's word.

title: keeps the clause in one cell
why: A semicolon in a phrase would end the clause early and the record test would read a stray one.

title: never writes pass
why: A row whose script stopped would be written as heard.

why: A script that listened for nothing would be written as heard.

why: A role with no words in the synonyms table would be wanted as nothing, and heard.
